items.title: Removed bullet margin-top may misalign badges
items.body: The `.bullet` `margin-top: 5px` was removed from `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper`, and `line-height: 1.5` was added. This presumably relies on the header's flex centering, but other contexts using `.extra-info-wrapper` could shift vertically. `order(2)` only takes effect if the parent is a flex container.

items.title: Flex layout disables the action button's right float
items.body: Making `.small-action` a flex container turns its direct children into flex items, and `float: right` on the button no longer positions it at the right edge. Since `.small-action-desc` also has no flex-grow or other rule to consume the remaining space, the button will sit immediately after the description instead of remaining right-aligned as before. Give the description a growing flex value or push the button with `margin-left: auto`.

items.title: Header panel alignment breaks under the prefixed flexbox the mixin enables
items.body: .panel lost float:right and now relies on margin-left:auto while .contents is turned into a flex container by the new flexbox() mixin, which emits display:-ms-flexbox and display:-webkit-box before display:flex. Those older flex models do not absorb auto margins, and once they apply, floats on flex items are ignored. In IE10 (and old WebKit that only honors the 2009 box syntax) the panel therefore stays next to the title instead of on the right. There is no float or justify-content fallback left in the rule.

items.title: 60s deadline for a batch of up to 100 external identity refreshes may break the reschedule chain
items.body: `check_auth_identities` refreshes up to `chunk_size=100` identities, and each refresh makes a network call to the SSO provider. It reschedules `check_auth` only at the end of the task. With the new 60s processing deadline, a slow provider can get the task killed before that point. The self-rescheduling chain then stops, and further auth checks depend on the periodic trigger. Raise the deadline or reschedule before processing the batch.

items.title: Project lookup changed from URL query param to replayRecord.project_id — but replayRecord may be undefined initially
items.body: The project lookup changed from useLocationQuery({fields: {project: decodeScalar}}) to useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}). If replayRecord is undefined (still loading), project_id is undefined, and useProjectFromId returns undefined. The query is disabled (enabled checks project?.slug), so no request fires. But the "Project not found" check (replayRecord?.project_id && !project) would be false (replayRecord?.project_id is undefined), so the error message doesn't show. When replayRecord loads, project_id becomes defined, and if the project isn't found, the error shows. This is correct behavior. But if replayRecord is undefined, the component falls through to isPending check — the useApiQuery isPending would be true (query disabled but still pending?), so the loading indicator shows. This is correct.

items.title: Feature flag only enabled for non-default strategy
items.body: createInitialDeployment() returns early when updateStrategy == null without enabling Profile.Feature.ROLLING_UPDATES, while the RECREATE path does enable it. Docs in this PR state the operator will fail while in preview unless rolling-updates is enabled, so the parameterized runs with null strategy will run without the required feature and fail or test the wrong configuration. Move the feature-enable block before the null early-return.

items.title: Default update-strategy tests never enable rolling-updates
items.body: createInitialDeployment returns immediately when updateStrategy is null, before the new FeatureSpec setup that enables rolling-updates. Both parameterized tests (testImageChange and testCacheMaxCount) include that null case, which is the documented default strategy. The operator guide in this PR states the preview feature must be enabled or the operator fails, so these cases deploy a CR without the feature and will not exercise (or will fail) the default upgrade path the test is meant to cover. Enable the feature before that return so every strategy, including the default, runs with rolling-updates.

items.title: Shifted override minutes wrap around midnight and get dropped
items.body: After adding the invitee/organizer offset, start and end are converted to minute-of-day via `hour()*60+minute()`. If the shift moves an override across the invitee's midnight (e.g. 22:00–02:00 in invitee time), endTime becomes smaller than startTime and `buildSlots` discards the range. `activeOverrides` is also still filtered on the unshifted `dayjs.utc(override.start)` date, so for large offsets the override can land on the wrong invitee day. Slots on the adjacent day are then missing or incorrect.

items.title: Split working hours incorrectly reject valid slots
items.body: The `.find()` rejects a slot if it is outside *any* working-hours interval on that day. With separate intervals such as 09:00–12:00 and 13:00–17:00, a 14:00 slot is rejected because it is outside the first interval, even though it fits the second. Check whether the slot fits at least one interval instead; otherwise users with split schedules lose valid availability.

items.title: Skip installer identity validation when the webhook has not created the integration yet
items.body: When no `Integration` row exists for this installation, this branch advances the pipeline without comparing `github_authenticated_user` to the installation sender. A delayed or missing installation webhook therefore lets the OAuth-authenticated user complete setup for an installation created by a different GitHub user, bypassing the identity check this change is meant to enforce.

items.title: BasePaginator silently clamps invalid forward offsets
items.body: src/sentry/api/paginator.py BasePaginator.get_result changed from queryset[offset:stop] to max(0,offset) for non-prev cursors. Other paginators in the same file explicitly reject offset<0 with BadPaginationError. Silently rewriting a tampered negative cursor to 0 returns the first page instead of an error, hiding invalid cursors and making pagination behavior inconsistent across paginators.

items.title: Tests mock the whole options module and depend on factory behavior, with no cache coverage
items.body: Mocking `options` makes every options.get return the allowlist, which affects unrelated lookups. The cache is never cleared between tests, and the key is identical for identical project sets, so tests can leak state. The caching, the invalidate function, and the top_events path are untested.

cal.com__8330.text: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime

Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))

discourse-graphite__5.text: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

keycloak__36882.text: Incorrect method call for exit codes. The picocli.exit() method calls System.exit() directly, which is problematic:
Need to add changelog/release notes documenting the exit code change and migration guidance

sentry-greptile__1.text: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.

When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.

sentry-greptile__3.text: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

sentry-greptile__5.text: The BrowserReportingCollectorEndpoint returns HttpResponse objects but the endpoint inherits from Endpoint which expects rest_framework.response.Response objects.
In BaseDetectorTypeValidator.update(), the validator incorrectly updates instance.type using validated_data.get('detector_type') instead of validated_data.get('type').

Using zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi result preserves the input order; dict value order is not guaranteed to match error_ids, so event data can be paired with the wrong ID (missing nodes also shift alignment).
Hardcoded empty data passed to TableWidgetVisualization causes it to always render an empty table instead of displaying actual results when the feature flag is enabled.

Validation logic incorrectly uses .get('timestamp'), which treats a timestamp of 0 as absent. It should directly check 'timestamp' in self.initial_data to ensure proper field presence detection, preventing both 'age=0' and 'timestamp' from passing mutual-exclusion validation.

Analytics events are recorded before the feature flag check, resulting in analytics being logged for all requests, including those that return 404 due to the feature being disabled. This can lead to misleading analytics data.

sentry__67876.text: Null reference if github_authenticated_user state is missing
OAuth state uses pipeline.signature (static) instead of a per-request random value

The code attempts to access integration.metadata[sender][login] without checking for the existence of the sender key. This causes a KeyError for integrations where the sender metadata was not set during creation
